input.question: Why didn't we actively re-center the ranges to follow the price (frequent narrowing), instead of staying wide?
input.reference: On 720 days 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, and the one live narrowing (31.08 to 11.09) ended -$32 vs HODL, so on 16.09 narrowing was rejected again because the upside (about +$1 per episode) is far smaller than the loss when the price leaves a ±5% range (about -$30).
input.answer: The project kept wide passive ranges because backtests showed active re-centering (narrowing) lost to passive wide strategies, even in flat regimes. The 720-day walkforward revealed that the extra fees earned by narrow ranges were more than offset by impermanent loss (IL) from frequent rebalancing. Specifically, the narrow strategy earned 4x more fees but ended with lower net returns because IL and re-centering costs consumed ~$1.9k–$2.9k more than the fee gains. The wide passive approach (±40–50%) consistently outperformed in both win rate and final PnL across different market regimes, including the flat periods where narrowing theoretically had an edge.

input.question: Why did the LP earn less in fees during an uptrend than in a flat market?
input.reference: Fees accrue only while the price is inside the range and fee yield scales roughly with 1/width, so a narrow range earns much more in a flat market but is left behind in a trend, while a wide range stays in range but earns several times less; the journal states this mechanism (the basis of FlatWide) but has no live measurement of fees during an uptrend, and it attributes the backtest losses in up windows to impermanent loss and LVR rather than to lower fees.
input.answer: In an uptrend, the LP position drifts out of its price range, so it stops earning trading fees while still suffering LVR (Loss-Versus-Rebalancing) from arbitrageurs trading against the stale price. In a flat market, the price stays within the range, allowing the LP to collect fees without large directional losses. The sources note that in UP windows, all strategies lost to HODL, whereas in FLAT windows, strategies won 58–100% of the time. The core issue is that fees do not cover the LVR incurred when the market trends away from the position's center.
